extracted.intended_audience: State Exchanges, SBE-FPs, QHP issuers, approved web-brokers/DE partners, and other stakeholders responding to HHS proposed rule and information collection requests
extracted.subtask_description: Extract and respond to proposed regulatory requirements and information-collection burdens for Health Insurance Exchanges (State Exchanges, FFE, SBE-FPs), QHP issuers, web-brokers, and related entities as described in the HHS proposed rule preamble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective Provider Access Review Program criteria (§155.1050(d)(2)-(d)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: States must satisfy applicable criteria to be considered to have an Effective Provider Access Review Program in order to conduct provider access reviews for issuers' plans that use and do not use a provider network.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a State demonstrates sufficient authority and technical capacity by satisfying the proposed criteria, it may perform provider access reviews for PY 2027 and beyond; otherwise HHS will continue Federal network adequacy reviews consistent with §156.230. HHS will continue to collect network adequacy data (including time and distance and appointment wait time) from all FFE issuers either for Federal review or to make available to States with an Effective Provider Access Review Program. The proposal anticipates negligible new data-collection burden because current systems/processes would be used, but burden may shift to the State-level depending on State implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Network adequacy data collection requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS will continue to collect network adequacy data, including time-and-distance and appointment wait time data, from all FFE issuers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data will be collected under existing OMB-approved collections (e.g., OMB Control Numbers 0938-1187 and 0938-1415). Data may be used for Federal reviews, or provided in a standardized format to States determined to have an Effective Provider Access Review Program to assist State-level analyses. HHS does not expect new burdens because it will utilize existing systems and processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: State Exchanges participation in SEIPM (State Exchange Improper Payment Measurement)
rubrics_metrics.description: SEIPM is a mandatory process for HHS to review payments of APTC that were determined by State Exchanges to produce an estimate of improper payments; State Exchanges would be required to participate and provide specified data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SEIPM is proposed to replace the prior IPPTA program. Participation entails multiple collections (Program Information, universe of tax households, review unit data). HHS will specify standardized data request forms and detailed specifications for formatting and submission; compliance must be consistent with OMB statistical sampling guidance for improper payment measurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of Program Information for SEIPM (§155.1615(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: State Exchanges must provide Program Information consisting of policy, operational and technical documentation concerning business rules and calculations, entity relationships, data dictionaries, operating procedures, and system technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This information is currently retained digitally and can be electronically transmitted; HHS estimates the burden associated with collection and transfer of this information would be no more than 40 hours per State Exchange.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of universe of tax household information for SEIPM (§155.1615(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: State Exchanges must provide HHS with a listing of the population of tax households enrolled in a QHP where APTC payments were made, including an identifier for each tax household, identifier for each QHP policy within that household, tax household size, total payment amounts for each sampled unit, and information about existence of an eligibility verification inconsistency for each sampled unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Burden associated with collection includes time to meet with HHS to review the submitted information; HHS estimates this burden would be no more than 40 hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review unit data elements required for SEIPM (§155.1615(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: For each sampled QHP tax household, State Exchanges must provide detailed review-unit data including monthly enrollment premium amounts, monthly APTC payment amounts, monthly Second Lowest Cost Silver Plan Premium amounts, monthly essential health benefit amounts; issuer-provided enrollment reconciliation info (effectuation payments, payment amounts, policy dates); SEP eligibility evidence; timing and coverage area of QHP certification; per-person attestation/demographics; electronic and manual eligibility verification details and documentary evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS anticipates using a standardized data request form with required fields; baseline burden estimated at up to 8 hours per sample (with economies of scale reducing average burden), and each State Exchange to provide between 50 and 250 samples proportionate to APTC volume. Final collection instrument/methodology will be provided in subsequent guidance to minimize burden while ensuring data quality and consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEIPM sampling and statistical requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial SEIPM sample sizes per State Exchange are expected to range between 50 and 250 samples, with an aggregate total sample size of approximately 2000 tax households across all State Exchanges; sample sizes may be adjusted over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjustments to total sample size may be driven by observed error rates, statistical precision requirements, State participation levels, and available resources, while ensuring compliance with OMB statistical sampling guidance for improper payment measurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEIPM burden, cost-estimation methodology, and per-sample assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS's burden estimate assumes an initial baseline of 8 hours per sample, later reduced by economies of scale to an average burden of 4.49 hours per sample; mean hourly rate across roles calculated as $111.12, producing an estimated cost per sample of approximately $499.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS details occupational wage assumptions (list of five occupational median wages), task analysis phases (setup, query development, sampling, review, closeout), and shows how aggregate cost ($1,097,800 across 22 Exchanges) is computed (2200 samples × $499). These are presented as estimates and HHS seeks comment on assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: State Exchanges burden estimates and economies of scale for SEIPM
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS expects significant economies of scale after initial sample due to established queries, trained personnel, standardized templates, and streamlined workflows; therefore per-sample burden should decrease after the initial setup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 8-hour baseline is described as the maximum expected burden per sample; actual average burden may fall to 4.49 hours as processes mature. HHS used standard Federal data collection burden estimation methodologies and a task analysis to derive estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrective Action Plans (CAPs) requirement following SEIPM (§155.1535 / future rulemaking)
rubrics_metrics.description: Selected State Exchanges may be required to develop and submit corrective action plans (CAPs) following a completed SEIPM measurement to reduce improper payments resulting from eligibility determination errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS estimates it could take each selected State Exchange up to 1,000 hours to develop a CAP. Using a management analyst rate of $97.30/hour, HHS estimates cost per State Exchange up to $97,300 and up to $2,140,600 across 22 Exchanges. CAP-related information collection will be submitted to OMB after future rulemaking on CAP process/requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitting SEIPM completion to satisfy annual independent external programmatic audit requirements (§155.1200)
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS proposes to amend §155.1200 to allow a State Exchange to satisfy certain annual independent external programmatic audit requirements by completing the required annual SEIPM program process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change is intended to reduce duplication between SEIPM and existing programmatic audit requirements, lowering external audit contracting costs (HHS projects roughly $45,000 annual cost reduction per State Exchange based on an estimated average audit cost of $150,000), while introducing the SEIPM-related data-submission burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discontinuation of standardized plan options and associated display/deviation rules (§155.20, §155.205(b)(1), §§155.220/156.265)
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS proposes to remove the definition of 'standardized options' and all associated standardized plan option requirements and differential display requirements; existing deviation requests from web-brokers and DE partners are reviewed based on whether the same or similar level of differentiation and clarity is provided as on HealthCare.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If finalized, removal would eliminate the need for entities to submit deviation requests for alternate differentiation formats; HHS anticipates requesting discontinuation of related ICRs (e.g., OMB Control Number 0938-1329). HHS seeks comment on burden estimates and assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discontinuation of non-standardized plan option limits and exceptions (§156.202)
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS proposes to discontinue non-standardized plan option limits and the exceptions process so issuers can offer plans tailored to chronic and high-cost conditions without submitting exception information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If finalized, HHS anticipates requesting discontinuation of the corresponding ICR (Non-Standardized Plan Option Limit Exceptions OMB Control Number: 0938-1461). HHS seeks comment on burden and compliance impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: ECP minimum percentage thresholds and requirement to designate contracted ECPs (§156.235)
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS proposes reducing the minimum percentage requirements for ECP thresholds from 35 percent to 20 percent for the overall, FQHC, and family planning ECP thresholds; issuers would still be required to designate contracted ECPs included within their provider networks in MPMS to meet the standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS states that the change would not alter the type of ECP data collected but may reduce issuer burden because fewer contracts may be needed to demonstrate compliance. HHS provides analysis of PY 2025 data indicating how many additional QHPs/SADPs would meet thresholds under a 20% standard and quantifies time savings from MPMS UI improvements (prepopulated ECPs, drop-down negotiation statuses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Modification of narrative justification requirements for ECP certification
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS proposes amending narrative justification language so narrative justifications are no longer required for issuers not meeting the ECP standard because they now input contract statuses directly into the ECP UI in MPMS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPMS improvements (prepopulation, drop-downs, identification of required fields) have reduced burden; HHS provides estimated time per ECP under prior Excel format (≈2 minutes) vs. MPMS drop-down (≈5 seconds), and describes how these UI changes reduce issuer administrative time during certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective ECP Review Program criteria for FFE States (§155.1051)
rubrics_metrics.description: FFE States (including those performing plan management) may elect to conduct their own ECP certification reviews if they demonstrate sufficient authority and technical capacity and submit an attestation; HHS will grant an Effective ECP Review Program designation upon determining that the State meets applicable requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a State is designated Effective ECP Review Program, HHS would not perform the ECP certification reviews for issuers in that State; issuers would still submit ECP data to HHS, but extensive Federal-level ECP corrections/resubmissions might be avoided. However, burden savings at the Federal level could be offset by State-level review burdens depending on how States implement procedures; HHS is uncertain how many States will elect to participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: QHP certification criteria for non-network plans (§156.236) — provider access sufficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-network plans seeking QHP certification must demonstrate they ensure a sufficient choice of providers consistent with sections 1311(c)(1)(B) and (C) of the Affordable Care Act and meet provider access sufficiency standards described at proposed §156.236.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §156.236 requires non-network plans to (a) report the assessed percentage of providers in a service area that accept the plan's benefit amount as payment in full, and (b) attest to a list of questions (§156.236(b)(4)-(9)) indicating they have processes/methodologies for continuous outreach to providers, public availability of benefit amounts, determination of benefit amounts, consumer-friendly information about balance billing/out-of-pocket costs, an exceptions process for enrollees who cannot find providers willing to accept the benefit amount, and adequate customer service or online provider-directory assistance. HHS estimates attestation will take approximately 30 seconds to 1 minute per question (max ~6 minutes per plan) and believes the additional time/cost is negligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: ECP data submission requirements for non-network plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-network plans applying for QHP certification must submit ECP data in MPMS demonstrating compliance with ECP-related requirements analogous to network plans, including meeting minimum percentages of available ECPs that accept the plan's benefit amount, offering the benefit amount to at least one ECP in each of the eight ECP categories per county, and offering the benefit amount to all available Indian health care providers in the service area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-network plans will use MPMS to select prepopulated ECPs and will indicate modified statuses (offered/accepted benefit amount as payment in full) rather than contract statuses. HHS does not believe these requirements impose significantly new information collections, given MPMS streamlining and similarity to current network-plan ECP data collection processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: QIS (Quality Improvement Strategy) data collection — no change
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no information collection associated with the proposed QIS policy and no changes are proposed to QIS data collection requirements applicable to QHP issuers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: QIS data collection from QHP issuers to the Exchange remains approved under OMB Control Number 0938-1286; HHS indicates no new burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uncertainty about State-level burden shifting and implementation variability
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS recognizes that while certain proposals may reduce Federal-level burdens (e.g., allowing State-conducted reviews), burden costs saved at the Federal level may be lost at the State review level depending on State implementation; total burden is therefore uncertain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS repeatedly notes uncertainty regarding how many States will elect to conduct reviews (Provider Access, ECP), how they would implement data collection and certification reviews, and therefore cannot precisely estimate total burden shifts between Federal and State levels; HHS seeks comment on these assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and approval standard for DE partner/display deviations
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests from web-brokers and QHP issuers seeking approval of an alternate differentiation format (deviation from HealthCare.gov standardized display) are reviewed based on whether the same or a similar level of differentiation and clarity is provided under the requested deviation as is provided on HealthCare.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the substantive standard HHS will apply when considering deviation requests; if the standardized option rules are removed, HHS anticipates discontinuing the related ICR because the deviation process would no longer be required.
